qualification: Published v0.4.8 -> v0.4.9 Helm chart pair on one disposable single-node Kind cluster (Kubernetes 1.36.1) on macOS arm64 under OrbStack. Local evaluation route: bundled PostgreSQL StatefulSet and bundled Keycloak. Fresh v0.4.8 installation, so portable lineage (0011-0018 -> 0019). Logical recovery set on the same host. The restore and the clean second upgrade ran in a second namespace in external-database mode with packaged Keycloak, because that is the only restore procedure the guide gives.

findings: OPERATIONS.md 'Bounded write-quiescing backup' waits on -l app.kubernetes.io/name=keycloakx, but the chart's Keycloak pods carry app.kubernetes.io/name=keycloak. kubectl wait --for=delete with no match returns at once with exit 0, so the documented stop step passes while Keycloak still holds connections. Only the next step's zero-connection check catches it, and only if the operator stops on a nonzero count. Fixed in the v0.4.10 chart guide (#164)

The guide gives no same-mode Kubernetes restore. Its only restore procedure targets an independent PostgreSQL with the chart in external mode, and the DBA's provisioning commands for that target are left to the fixture (synveda-database-bootstrap with a newline-terminated roles.json). A bundled installation restored this way changes ownership mode

helm upgrade undid the manual scale-down at apply time (gateway, worker and Keycloak back to 1) with no SSA conflict. The guide says not to rely on that and to start Keycloak first; in practice all three started beside the install Job. The new gateway and worker crash-looped until the stamp; after a long Job the worker's CrashLoopBackOff delay held full readiness 144 s past Job completion

The release image overlay changes the PostgreSQL and Keycloak digests while OPERATIONS.md says to keep them fixed on application-only upgrades. Passing the target overlay left PostgreSQL on the v0.4.8 image (OnDelete) and moved Keycloak to v0.4.9's image (its pod was recreated by the scale-up). The guide does not say which overlay the upgrade takes

helm rollback recreated the deleted v0.4.8 install Job, so the previous migrator ran again (it refused at preflight on 3 pods and wrote nothing). helm rollback without --wait reports success while the previous gateway and worker refuse readiness

A SIGKILLed migrator client left its server backend waiting and holding the advisory boundary and two AccessExclusive locks for about 9.5 s; its disappearance at about 10 s is consistent with the server-side lock bound in the phase table
Operator preflight fails on kubectl client/server skew with OrbStack's bundled kubectl 1.33.9 against Kind 1.36.1; the README asks for a client within one minor and qualifies 1.36.1
The writer-drain wait is not logged in the Job: the migrate container prints only the final refusal, not the 'waiting for gateway and worker database sessions' warning
